# OpenNetworkDesignTokens — Swift (iOS, iPadOS, macOS)

A Swift package: `OpenNetworkDesignTokens` holds every value with no dependency (it builds and tests on Linux too); `SwiftUI.swift` adds the bindings where SwiftUI exists.

```swift
import OpenNetworkDesignTokens

RootView()
    .ndTheme(.light, direction: .on, platform: .ios, density: .comfortable)

struct Title: View {
    @Environment(\.ndColors) private var colors
    var body: some View {
        Text("NDDev").ndText(.h1).foregroundStyle(colors.textPrimary.color)
    }
}
```

- Colours: `NDColors.resolve(theme:direction:)` (sRGB). Increase Contrast (`colorSchemeContrast == .increased`) selects `.darkContrast` / `.lightContrast`.
- Metrics in points: `NDMetrics.resolve(platform:density:)`; targets are 44 pt on iOS.
- Text: `NDTextStyle.resolve(_:platform:script:)` scales with the Dynamic Type style it names; set `\.ndScript` from the locale (Arabic and Chinese drop tracking and case).
- Motion: `NDDurations` take `.reduced` when Reduce Motion is on (`accessibilityReduceMotion`).
- Icons and the mark: `NDVectorImage(.arrow)`, `NDVectorImage(NDBrand.mark)` draw in the foreground style, fitted to their frame (decorative, hidden from accessibility).
- Fonts: the package bundles IBM Plex Sans and IBM Plex Sans Arabic (400, 500, 600; OFL-1.1, licence in `Fonts/`); call `NDBundledFonts.register()` once at launch. Chinese and monospace use the system faces (PingFang SC; SF Mono, else Menlo).
- Tint: where system chrome tints its material or selection (`.tint`), it takes the direction's `accent.brand`; text and icons on system materials keep the system label colours (ADR 0006).
